claim: *Obligations and permitted realizations.* The obligations jointly admit an acceptable region; the controls jointly permit another. Where permitted exceeds acceptable, unacceptable realizations slip through — underconstraint; where acceptable exceeds permitted, acceptable alternatives are excluded — overconstraint.
topology: Two overlapping sets; acceptable-only, intersection, permitted-only retain left/center/right spatial meaning.
bw_encoding: Black strokes and text; pale gray headers only. Dashed paths retain optional, missing, or forbidden semantics where explicitly labeled. Position, containment, line weight, and written labels carry distinctions without color.
redesign: Native nodes and routed edges preserve the original semantic structure, with print-sized labels and fewer decorative frames.
alt:
A bounding panel holds the software realization space. Inside it, two overlapping
    rectangles: a solid one for the acceptable realizations, those satisfying every obligation, and a
    dashed one for the realizations the controls permit. Their overlap is the preserved freedom —
    acceptable and permitted. The acceptable-only region at left is overconstraint: acceptable
    alternatives excluded. The permitted-only region at right is underconstraint:
    unacceptable, yet permitted — a correctness risk.
